definition: A Python-embedded language for writing high-performance GPU kernels without raw CUDA, powering much of the open custom-kernel ecosystem (FlashAttention variants, quantization kernels).
details: A Python-embedded language for writing high-performance GPU kernels without raw CUDA, powering much of the open custom-kernel ecosystem (FlashAttention variants, quantization kernels). Not to be confused with NVIDIA's Triton Inference Server, which is a serving system.

explainer.lead: Triton is a Python-embedded language for writing high-performance GPU kernels without raw CUDA, powering much of the open custom-kernel ecosystem. It matters because it lets engineers write fast GPU code with far less low-level CUDA work.

tiers.eli5: Instead of hand-writing machine-level instructions for a graphics chip, you write Python-like code and Triton translates it into fast GPU instructions.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use Triton for custom kernels such as FlashAttention variants and quantization kernels; a common pitfall is confusing it with NVIDIA's Triton Inference Server, which is a serving system, not a kernel language.
tiers.paperLevel: Triton is defined as a Python-embedded language for writing high-performance GPU kernels without raw CUDA; it powers much of the open custom-kernel ecosystem, including FlashAttention variants and quantization kernels.

explainer.example: An engineer writes a fused attention kernel in Triton instead of CUDA, and it is used as a FlashAttention-style building block.
